$comment: Generated. Ungraded check of prior knowledge before Module 1; each item's lesson is its module number, so support is set module by module.

items.stem: What makes an AI agent different from a chatbot?

options.text: It always runs on a bigger language model
It replies faster than a chatbot
It can decide on steps and use tools to act toward a goal

items.stem: Which job is best handled by a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Emailing the same stock report every Monday at 8 AM
Looking into a customer's problem across several systems
Answering open questions about orders, returns and exchanges

items.stem: A language model writes its answer by…

options.text: Predicting the next piece of text, one token at a time
Looking each answer up in a database of facts
Running the code you send it

items.stem: What is a system prompt for?

options.text: Setting the model's role, rules and the facts it should use
Storing the user's password
Choosing which computer runs the model

items.stem: When an agent "calls a tool", who actually runs the tool?

options.text: The customer runs it in their browser
The language model runs it inside itself
Your code runs it and sends the result back to the model

items.stem: A tool call fails with a timeout. What should your code send back to the model?

options.text: Nothing, so the model doesn't get confused
An empty result
A clear error message, marked as an error

items.stem: Between two API calls, what does the model remember about your conversation?

options.text: Only what you send again in the messages
Always the last three messages
Everything from earlier calls, automatically

items.stem: What does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) add to an agent?

options.text: Relevant text from your own documents, put into the prompt
A way to train a new model from scratch
A faster model

items.stem: You're building your first agent. What's the best way to start?

options.text: Get the smallest loop working, then add one tool at a time
Give it every tool you might ever need on day one
Write the whole system before running anything

items.stem: How do you know whether an agent is good enough to launch?

options.text: The model provider says the model is accurate
It answered your three favourite questions well
You run it on a set of test cases and look at what fails

items.stem: Which guardrail stops an agent from looping all weekend on a failing tool?

options.text: A step limit and a spend limit on every request
A larger context window
A friendlier system prompt

items.stem: Where should your API key live when you put an agent online?

options.text: On the server, in an environment variable
In the system prompt
In the web page's JavaScript
